Commentary.Commentary: We are back with England's reply! The umpires are out and are followed by the explosive batting pair of Will Jacks and Phil Salt. West Indies spread across the field and skipper Rovman Powell hands the ball to Romario Shepherd who will start the proceedings for them. Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With the dew setting in, bowling will be an even tougher challenge for West Indies, especially given the track record at this venue. Defending 145 runs won't be easy, and they'll have to produce an extraordinary effort to contain England's powerful batting lineup. England, on the other hand, will look to keep it straightforward and aim to wrap up the game and the series, without unnecessary drama. An exciting chase awaits, so stay tuned!

Jamie Overton is down for a quick chat. He says that a couple of back stress fractures is not good but he is happy to be back and bowling. Adds that he was rested in the last game and it was just precautionary as his body feels good now. Mentions that it is all about hitting the right areas and the top of off. Ends by saying that there is a bit of tennis ball like bounce on this wicket but hopes they will chase this down.

Skipper Rovman Powell joined forces with Romario Shepherd to stabilize the innings and build a crucial partnership. The experienced duo counterattacked the spinners, rescuing the West Indies from dire straits and forging a solid 73-run stand. However, Jamie Overton's return to the attack proved decisive, as he struck twice in a single over to swing the momentum back in England’s favour. Alzarri Joseph's quickfire 21 runs propelled West Indies to 145 runs which is certainly a decent score considering how the innings started. For England, Saqib Mahmood led the charge with three early wickets, while Overton claimed three towards the end. Powell’s fighting 54 was the bright spot, giving the West Indies bowlers something to defend.

After winning the toss again and choosing to bowl first, England had a dream start as Jacob Bethell’s superb throw in the opening over dismissed Shai Hope. From there, things unravelled quickly for the hosts. Saqib Mahmood and Jofra Archer tore through the West Indies' top order, reducing them to a dismal 39/5 by the end of the Powerplay. In this must-win match, the West Indies batters crumbled under pressure, giving away their wickets and plunging themselves into deeper trouble.

It’s been a commendable recovery from the West Indies to get to 145/8, with Alzarri Joseph adding crucial late runs to turn what seemed like a below-par total into something far more competitive. While they may still be short of an ideal score, they’ve kept themselves firmly in the contest. This game is far from over!

Commentary.Commentary: Bashes the deck hard, on a back of a length, on middle, Rovman Powell tucks it to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Jofra Archer to Rovman Powell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Gorgeous shot! Fuller in length, outside off, shaping away further, Rovman Powell leans on and lofts his shot over cover for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Jofra Archer to Rovman Powell, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Short and down leg, Rovman Powell hops inside the line and lets it go past.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Jofra Archer to Rovman Powell, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: In the air, but safe! Fires it full, on middle and leg, Rovman Powell looks to flick but closes the bat face a bit too early. Gets an outside edge that balloons over the bowler and plugs in the vacant region behind mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Saqib Mahmood to Rovman Powell, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Immediately drags the length back, just outside off, Rovman Powell looks to pull but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Saqib Mahmood to Rovman Powell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Saqib Mahmood is overcompensating and trying to find that swing but is punished this time by Powell! Fuller and on off, Rovman Powell cream it through covers for a boundary to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Saqib Mahmood to Rovman Powell, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length on off, Rovman Powell pushes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Saqib Mahmood to Rovman Powell, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rovman Powell walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust and Saqib Mahmood's happiness knows no bounds! West Indies are falling like a pile of cards in the Powerplay! Saqib Mahmood lands this wider on off, fuller in length and gets the ball to shape away off the deck, Roston Chase has a swing at it but plays away from the body and manages to only find an outside edge that goes straight into the hands of Jamie Overton at first slip.
Commentary.Howout: c Jamie Overton b Saqib Mahmood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Saqib Mahmood to Roston Chase, OUT! c Jamie Overton b Saqib Mahmood.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Classic shot! A bit too full from Mahmood, on off, Roston Chase firms his drive to perfection through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Saqib Mahmood to Roston Chase, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short one, on leg, Shimron Hetmyer ducks under and lets it go.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Shimron Hetmyer, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shimron Hetmyer is the next man in with West Indies in a spot of bother.

OUT! CLEANED'EM UP! Jofra Archer joins the party and gets the biggest fish in the West Indian lineup! Nicholas Pooran goes back for 7(4) and West Indies slip further down to 17/3! Angling in, on a hard length, into the stumps, Nicholas Pooran has a wild swing across the line but fails to get any connection. The ball skids through and goes past the bat on the inside edge and pegs down the middle stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Nicholas Pooran, OUT! b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, outside off, Roston Chase leans on and drives it past cover. Sam Curran gives the ball a good chase and pulls it back in time, keeping it down to three runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Fired in a yorker, on off, Roston Chase digs it out to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just short of Liam Livingstone! Angling in, on a back of a length, over off, Roston Chase miscues his punch over the infield on the on side and chips it just in front of mid on. Liam Livingstone dives ahead but cant get to it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, over middle and off, Nicholas Pooran gets on top of his toes and pushes it to third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Nicholas Pooran, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, on off, Roston Chase taps it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Saqib Mahmood to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Continues to keep the length short and on off, Roston Chase covers the line and blocks it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Saqib Mahmood to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, over off, Roston Chase dabs it down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Saqib Mahmood to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Roston Chase comes out to the middle now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Saqib Mahmood makes an immediate impact! England gets two in successive overs and West Indies are in all sorts of trouble, way early in the inning! Saqib Mahmood dishes it on a good length, just around off, Evin Lewis misreads the length and goes for the pull shot on a ball that was not that short in length. Gets an outside edge that goes straight in front of deep third where Jofra Archer settles under and takes it with both hands in front of his face.
Commentary.Howout: c Jofra Archer b Saqib Mahmood
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Saqib Mahmood to Evin Lewis, OUT! c Jofra Archer b Saqib Mahmood.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling across, on a fuller length, outside off, Evin Lewis slashes hard and gets it off the toe end of the bat. Skies it over to the right of deep third for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Saqib Mahmood to Evin Lewis, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Steams in from over the wicket and hurls it on a good length, on middle, Evin Lewis taps it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Saqib Mahmood to Evin Lewis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Saqib Mahmood to share the attack.
SIX! Wow, what a way to get off the mark! Jofra Archer digs it in short and on middle, Nicholas Pooran reads the length early and nails his pull over square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Nicholas Pooran, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on off, Nicholas Pooran tucks it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Nicholas Pooran, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicholas Pooran walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! RUN OUT! Extraordinary throw from Jacob Bethell and Shai Hope has to go back for just 4(2) giving England an early advantage! Back of a length from Archer, on middle and leg, very similar to the previous delivery, Shai Hope hops back and tucks it in front of square leg and sets off for the run. Evin Lewis sends him back from halfway down the track and Jacob Bethell hits the single stump he had his eyes set on. Hope is miles away from making it back into the crease and walks off without even waiting for the third umpire's decision.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, OUT! run out (Jacob Bethell).

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Great ball but West Indies and Shai Hope get a boundary off it! Shaping in, on a hard length, over middle and leg, almost cut Hope in two halves. Shai Hope just looks to jam it out and gets an inside edge past the stumps and to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and angling into the batter, on middle and leg, Evin Lewis swivels and pulls off the outer half of his bat, aerially to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Evin Lewis, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from around the wicket and lands it on a good length, outside off, Evin Lewis looks to ride the bounce and cut it away but ends up chopping it down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Evin Lewis, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the England players spread out and take their respective field positions. Evin Lewis and Shai Hope are the two openers for West Indies. Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. First up, it will be St. Lucia's national anthem followed by the national anthem of England. Finally, it will conclude with the Rally 'Round the West Indies.

Rovman Powell, the captain of West Indies says that they have talked about their shortcomings and it is all about clarity. Adds that if they let England score big again in the Powerplay without taking wickets, they will be behind in the game. Says that if they do well in that phase, the middle overs will take care of themselves. Informs that they have three changes due to a few niggles here and there. Alzarri Joseph comes back in the team, and so do Shimron Hetmyer and Shai Hope.

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England says with the kind of weather around, they are looking to chase. Adds that they need to start well again despite this being a good wicket. Concludes that they have one change in the side with Adil Rashid missing out and Rehan Ahmed coming in.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Shai Hope (In place of Brandon King), Nicholas Pooran (WK), Rovman Powell (C), Shimron Hetmyer (In place of Sherfane Rutherford), Roston Chase, Romario Shepherd, Alzarri Joseph (In place of Matthew Forde), Gudakesh Motie, Akeal Hosein, Terrance Hinds.

England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt (WK), Will Jacks, Jos Buttler (C), Liam Livingstone, Jacob Bethell, Sam Curran, Dan Mousley, Jamie Overton, Rehan Ahmed (In place of Adil Rashid), Jofra Archer, Saqib Mahmood.
TOSS - The coin goes up in the air and Jos Buttler calls it right again. England have elected to BOWL first.

UPDATE - 8.21 pm GMT, Previous Day - Good news at last! All the covers are off and the players are heading out for warm-up drills. We now have a confirmed TOSS TIME as well – it’s set for 8.30 pm GMT (Previous Day) with the match set to begin 15 minutes later.

UPDATE - 8.07 pm GMT, Previous Day - The two umpires were out to the middle a little while ago for an inspection. Most of the covers are off now but the pitch is still under a big cover. Perhaps they are concerned about a dark cloud hovering above the ground and taking a precautionary measure. However, the umpires are still not satisfied with the condition of the outfield and we will have to wait for a bit long. Also, we have 60 minutes of buffer time before we start losing any overs.

Just In - The news coming from the England camp is that Reece Topley has been ruled out for the remainder of this series due to the knee injury he picked up in the opening game. Yet another setback for him, it seems like he just can't catch a break. Also, he has been fined by the ICC for smashing a chair showing his frustration while leaving the ground in the first match.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is alongside Carlos Brathwaite for the Pitch analysis. Nikhil says all the games played at this venue have been won by the teams chasing and adds that this has been a high-scoring venue. Mentions the dimensions and says that the square boundaries are 63 meters while the straight boundary is 71 meters but wind will be a crucial factor to consider. Brathwaite joins him and mentions that there is even covering of grass and if the bowlers hit the right areas around the 6-8 meter mark, they will get a good purchase. Adds that the batters will enjoy and we can expect a high-scoring encounter.

Romario Shepherd is up for a flash interview. He says that they need to execute with the ball better and also do well with the bat as well. Adds that it is a big difference to bowl under lights and wind plays a big factor at this ground. Mentions that Russell not being here gives him a lot more responsibility. Ends by saying that Dre Russ is a big miss as he can have an impact with both bat and ball but now he has to pull up his socks for the team in Russell's absence.

UPDATE - 7.43 pm GMT, Previous Day - It is not raining currently now but due to the overnight rain there were a few wet patches in the outfield. The umpires are concerned about that and the ground staff are working on it to get the ground ready as soon as possible.

Liam Livingstone is down for a chat. He says this pitch could play better while the toss was crucial in the first two games. Adds that there is a bit more pace and bounce here which is good for everybody and they are looking forward to playing here. Mentions the depth they have as a side and says there are a lot of exciting players coming up. Concludes that the last 6 months have been great for him and he looks to continue and win games for his team while enjoying the game.

UPDATE - 7.33 pm GMT, Previous Day - Well, the toss should have been done by now but it has started to rain in St. Lucia. The covers are on at the moment and the toss is officially delayed. We hope it is just a passing shower and we get some action soon.

The weather is slightly overcast, but we remain optimistic that it won't play spoilsport in what promises to be a thrilling contest. With the series potentially on the line, both teams are set to give it their all, leaving no room for error. England, riding high on form and momentum, will be a tough nut to crack, but West Indies will be determined to fight back, reclaim their confidence, and keep the series alive. Stay tuned as the toss and team updates are just around the corner - this is a match you won’t want to miss!

England, on the other hand, have been clinical in both matches, asserting their dominance with well-rounded performances. The return of Jos Buttler, not just as captain but as a dynamic batter, was a game-changer in the previous match, where he made a storming comeback after a tough first game. His presence strengthens an already fierce and in-form batting lineup, posing a significant challenge for the West Indies bowlers. On the bowling front, England may consider a couple of changes. John Turner could be in line for his T20I debut if England decide to rest Jofra Archer and if Reece Topley remains sidelined due to the injury he sustained in the first game.

West Indies have struggled to carry their momentum from the ODI series win, with their top-order batting proving to be a significant concern in the first two T20Is. Traditionally, the West Indies have been a powerhouse with the bat in the shortest format, and it’s hard to imagine them not bouncing back to their trademark aggressive style. However, with the series on the line, the urgency to deliver has never been higher. The return of Alzarri Joseph into the squad will add much-needed balance to the side, bolstering both their bowling and overall confidence.

Hello and a warm welcome to the third T20I between West Indies and England, coming to you from the Daren Sammy National Cricket Stadium in St Lucia! England have stormed to a 2-0 lead in the series with dominant performances, leaving the hosts, West Indies, in a must-win situation entering this match. With the series on the line, the West Indies will be banking on this change of venue to turn their fortunes around. Meanwhile, England will be looking to maintain their momentum and close out the series with another commanding display.
... MATCH DAY ...

What a return to form for English skipper Jos Buttler as he led his side to a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series against West Indies and with the Barbados leg of the tour done and dusted, the teams now move to Gros Islet in St. Lucia for the remainder of the matches. Hosts West Indies did pip the ODI series 2-1 against an undercooked English team but now, with their stellar T20I lineup, they just haven't managed to do the damage with the bat which really is concerning and the loss of Andre Russell due to injury is a big blow to them as well. The top order has been the main culprit with the likes of Brandon King and Evin Lewis just not firing and Nicholas Pooran hasn't been able to replicate his form from a few months back. Shai Hope who was prolific in the ODI series has been on the bench and maybe it is time, the Windies give the ODI skipper a chance in the T20 format as well. One positive for West Indies is the return of Alzarri Joseph from suspension after his antics in the ODI series and he will be back with more fire and hunger. However, Gudakesh Motie and Akeal Hosein will have to play a big role if the Windies are to stay alive in the series. England on the other hand have looked solid with the bat as the top order has fired in both games. Phil Salt made a century in the first game followed by Buttler's 83 in the 2nd game. The likes of Will Jacks and Jacob Bethell too have contributed with the bat, and that destructive middle order hasn't even had the chance which is not good signs for West Indies. England did lose Reece Topley due to an injury in the first game but Jofra Archer took his place in the following match and it has been Saqib Mahmood who has been doing the damage in those early overs allowing someone like Adil Rashid to then come in and control the middle phase. The odds are highly stacked up against the hosts but it is a different venue which they know better and this could be the one game they need to turn things around but it won't be easy against and upbeat England lineup. Who are you backing for the win?
